I pressed my palms against one of the elephants,
trying to imagine the incredible heat that forged the stone.
Marina began climbing, using the crevices in the rock to
hoist herself up. She reached the top, about twenty feet
above me, before she looked down and grinned. I grinned
back, marveling at how well my sister and I were getting
along here at Elephant Rocks State Park.
The Surprising Allure of Slow TV
In 2009, Norway’s public broadcasting station, NRK,
unexpectedly launched: a new national pastime, slow TV.
NRK producers aired the seven-hour, fourteen-minute
“Bergensbanen Minute by Minute.” It showed continuous
footage of the 309-mile Bergensbanen train route from
Oslo, the capital, to Bergen, a city on Norway’s west coast.
Expecting only about 2,000 viewers, the producers
were shocked when 1.2 million Norwegians tuned in. Both
the station and social media was flooded with suggestions
